title: Tenant-scoped RBAC-aware audit partitioning and SAML role enrichment
creator: Avery Chen
description: Scope: Add RBAC-aware enrichment to the audit ingestion pipeline so every audit event can be correlated to SSO/SAML-derived roles and to tenant-scoped admin controls, and then store events using an adaptive partitioning/indexing scheme that limits storage/query cost while preserving fast lookups for admin investigations and compliance. Background: RBAC v2 rollouts and SSO mappings mean we can attribute actions to role sets (e.g., org-admin, billing-admin, infra-admin). Current audit storage is log-sharded by time only; high-cardinality role/tenant searches are expensive and leave cold storage queries that blow cost. This ticket implements a pipeline stage that injects role attributes into event documents, computes a partition key that balances tenant, role, and time, and stores compact secondary indexes for short-term hot queries and long-term cold archives with TTL policies. Goals: 1) Make admin-action queries (by tenant + role + actor) < 300ms for last 30 days. 2) Reduce monthly audit query egress cost for 30-90 day windows by 35% vs current baseline. 3) Ensure retention and archival policies remain auditable and reversible for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion: role enrichment stage parses SAML assertions and maps to canonical role identifiers for >99% of events in staging
Partitioning: new partition key (tenant|role-hash|day) implemented; write distribution avoids >10% hot-shard skew across tenants in load test
Query perf: common admin investigation query (tenant + role + action type) returns results within 300ms for a 30-day window on production-like dataset
Cost: 30-90 day window query cost reduced by >=35% in benchmark compared to current baseline (same dataset)
Retention: retention policies (hot 30d, warm 120d, cold archive 365d) enforced by lifecycle job with observable metrics and documented rollback steps
Security controls: events marked with admin-sensitivity label and encrypted with tenant-scoped KMS key binding; security review signed off
Observability: dashboards showing partition skew, per-tenant ingest rate, enrichment success rate, and query latency are added to the audit-monitoring dashboard
tasks: Design enrichment schema and canonical role IDs (collab with Sec + IAM)
Implement SAML assertion parser module in ingestion pipeline (prototype in staging)
Define and implement partition key strategy and write adaptor for storage layer
Add compact secondary index for recent admin-action lookups (30d hot index)
Create lifecycle controller that migrates data between hot/warm/cold tiers and triggers compaction
Benchmarks: create synthetic workload and run cost/latency experiments
Add observability: ingestion metrics, enrichment success counters, per-partition cardinality gauges
Add KMS binding and mark admin events for tenant-scoped encryption; coordinate with security for key rotation plan
Write runbook for investigation queries and archive retrieval (for support and compliance)
decision_log: 2026-02-19: Chose tenant|role-hash|day partition key to balance time-series queries and role cardinality (vs tenant|hour which caused too many shards)
2026-02-26: Agreed to store canonical role IDs instead of full SAML payload to minimize index size
2026-03-03: Decided on hot 30d / warm 120d / cold 365d lifecycle tiers after cost modeling with Finance
risks: High-cardinality roles for large tenants could still create hot shards if a single tenant has thousands of role variants
Incorrect SAML mapping may misattribute actions; requires robust fallback and alerting
Encryption per-tenant increases KMS key usage and may add latency to writes if not cached
Archive retrieval for compliance could be slower if compaction/encoding is aggressive
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy enrichment and partitioning to a small subset of tenants, run synthetic load and validate enrichment accuracy
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% production traffic (low-risk tenants), monitor metrics and cost, iterate
Phase 3 (gradual): expand in 25% increments with automated fallback to time-only partitions if write latency exceeds threshold
Phase 4: full enablement and deprecation of legacy indices after 90 days of stable metrics
open_questions: How should we handle cross-tenant role references for shared-service accounts?
What is the acceptable false-positive rate for SAML role mapping before we trigger a rollback?
Do compliance teams want raw SAML assertions stored in cold archive for future audits?
Should queries against cold archives be served via a separate retrieval API with quota enforcement?
